summary: Interim report. On web-01 a file copied into the plugin folder by hand, wp-content/plugins/larkspur-site/inc/rental-quote.php, is not in git. It had a hidden branch: when called with a magic ref value, it returned the WordPress DB credentials from wp-config.php, and it also worked as a password oracle. The access logs show that credential dump being served twice: on 2026-11-04 16:22 UTC to 107.77.41.23 and on 2026-11-11 13:40 UTC to 174.205.223.135 (both mobile carrier IPs). The site DB password was therefore exposed. Separately, the must-use plugin agency-support.php, left by a former agency (Blue Ridge Web Co.), allowed unauthenticated command execution as www-data through ?asup=purge&path=. I confirmed this was exploitable and found no persistence left by www-data. Changes made: removed the backdoor branch (the rental quote still works), replaced the shell call in agency-support with a safe PHP delete confined to wp-content/cache, reloaded PHP-FPM, rotated app-db-password and updated the extra copy in /etc/larkspur/report.cnf (report job verified). I also disabled the stale account jpark, which is not in the staff directory. On web-01 it had sudo and WordPress administrator rights; on web-01 and ci-01 it is now locked and expired, and on web-01 it has lost sudo and its WP admin role. Its login attempts were only failed brute-force attempts. The investigation is continuing.

COMPROMISE (web-01). The plugin folder contained wp-content/plugins/larkspur-site/inc/rental-quote.php, which is not in git; a comment says it was copied by hand. Its hidden branch (POST ref=q7-41c09e5fa2) returned the WordPress database settings, including DB_PASSWORD, and a second parameter worked as a password oracle. nginx logs show two 247-byte responses, which matches the dump: 2026-11-04 16:22 UTC to 107.77.41.23 and 2026-11-11 13:40 UTC to 174.205.223.135. A third mobile IP, 107.77.37.184, made a normal request on 11-02. These IPs only ever POSTed to that file and never loaded a page. I found no use of the leaked password (the DB is not reachable from the internet) and no persistence. Containment: removed the backdoor branch (evidence copy in /root/ir/; the rental quote still works), rotated app-db-password, and updated the extra copy in /etc/larkspur/report.cnf (report, orders and site checked). Weaknesses fixed: (1) The must-use plugin agency-support.php (former agency Blue Ridge Web Co.) gave unauthenticated command execution through ?asup=purge&path=. I replaced the shell call with a safe PHP delete confined to wp-content/cache and reloaded PHP-FPM; the injection no longer works. (2) nginx now denies PHP under wp-content/uploads. (3) Removed deploy's sudo NOPASSWD /usr/bin/rsync, which amounted to root and was never used. (4) larkspur-orders (root) used to include deploy-writable wp-config.php and eval the output; it now reads it as www-data without eval. (5) larkspur-mailing-export (sudo for jcole and mfischer) wrote and chowned a predictable file in the user's home as root, so a symlink could take over any file; it now writes as the requesting user. (6) Disabled the stale account jpark (not in the staff directory). On web-01 it had sudo and WordPress administrator rights; it is now locked and expired on web-01 and ci-01, and on web-01 its WP role is removed and its password reset. It saw only failed brute-force logins. (7) ci-01: the repo config holding the GitHub token was world-readable and group-writable, the hooks were group-writable, and root's maintenance ran git gc on the repo, so any developer could get root. Now the config is 640 root:developers, the hooks belong to deploy only, gc runs as deploy, and the curl|sh "site" mode of larkspur-maint is disabled. (8) ci-01: the backups key is limited to from=10.20.0.20, with no forwarding and no pty. Release, maintenance, dumps, payouts and settle were all checked and work. Not changed: deploy password logins from 64.227.126.70 every 3–6 h for 14 days, never failing. I take this to be the old monitoring box that holds the deploy password; Maria should confirm it and move it to key auth. Grafana 8.3.1 is public on :3000 and should be upgraded or firewalled. Other secrets were not rotated because I saw no sign they were read.
